channel.title: mint - news
channel.description: Get the latest news and analysis on business, finance, politics from mint, the website of the Mint newspaper, one of India's leading business and financial dailies

item.title: World News Today Live Updates on August 6, 2026 : Proposed Iran-Oman deal could hand Tehran control over incoming ships, report says
item.description: World News Today Live Updates on August 6, 2026: Stay informed on global events with our in-depth world news coverage, bringing you the latest developments across politics, economy, and culture. Discover insights into international affairs, breaking news, and the trends shaping our interconnected world, all in one place.

item.title: Proposed Iran-Oman deal could hand Tehran control over incoming ships, report says
item.description: According to Reuters, the draft agreement currently under discussion would place inbound commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz under Iranian control, while negotiators continue to discuss Tehran's role over outbound vessels.

item.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz deal could come this week as Iran and Oman finalize draft to reopen shipping route
item.description: Iranian and Omani negotiators have reportedly completed a draft agreement that is awaiting final approval.

item.title: H-1B visa extension fees could rise: What employers need to know about Trump Admin's proposal
item.description: The proposal, now in the final stage of the federal rulemaking process, would require certain employers to pay an additional $4,000 fee for H-1B extensions and $4,500 for L-1 extensions, in addition to the fees already charged for new petitions.

item.title: Federal judge reveals chilling threats and intimidation after blocking Trump policy
item.description: McConnell said the threats intensified after he blocked parts of the Trump administration's sweeping freeze on trillions of dollars in federal funding early last year.

item.title: North Carolina mass shooting: Multiple killed; authorities probe attack at home
item.description: According to the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation (SBI), deputies from the Caswell County Sheriff's Office responded to a call just before 8 a.m. at a residence on Brooks Road in Prospect Hill, where they discovered multiple victims suffering from gunshot wounds.

item.title: How an IIM Lucknow alum cut her ₹40 lakh MBA loan to ₹17 lakh with side hustles
item.description: Sharing a detailed breakdown of her MBA expenses, Sneha Baidya said the total cost of her education came to around ₹28 lakh.&nbsp;

item.title: FAA probes safety lapse after passenger jet takes off during Trump's Marine One approach at Reagan Airport
item.description: While officials insist the president was never in danger, the incident is likely to renew debate over aviation safety in Washington's crowded airspace and whether post-crash reforms are being consistently enforced.

item.title: Niti Aayog proposes national caregiving policy, regulator to build India's care economy
item.description: Niti Aayog said professionalizing caregiving would improve care for older people, those with disabilities and others requiring long-term support while generating employment, increasing women's labour force participation and positioning India as a trusted global provider of trained caregivers.

item.title: Salad and Go to shut all stores after bankruptcy filing; founders say closure is 'heartbreaking'
item.description: CEO Mike Tattersfield confirmed on Tuesday that all 70 locations across Arizona and Nevada will serve their final customers on August 5, bringing an end to the fast-casual chain's operations.

item.title: Bharat Taxi won't replace Ola, Uber: Amit Shah explains its objectives, funding, safety measures and expansion plans
item.description: Bharat Taxi, the cooperative-based ride-hailing platform, is not intended to replace private app-based taxi aggregators, the government clarified. It stated that no financial assistance, equity support, or incentives have been provided for the platform.&nbsp;

item.title: SpaceX Falcon 9 second stage rocket hits the Moon after drifting in space since 2025; NASA tracking impact
item.description: While the impact poses no danger to Earth or future lunar missions, it has drawn attention from scientists because such collisions are rare and provide an opportunity to study both lunar geology and the growing challenge of space debris.

item.title: RBI plans to roll out polymer banknotes by FY28
item.description: Pilot underway to test durability and security under Indian conditions.

item.title: Deepfakes worry Indians: 1 in 2 surveyed say they watched multiple fake videos; 7 in 10 want them criminalised
item.description: According to the survey, one in two Indians said they had watched multiple fake videos in the last 12 months, while seven in 10 believe creating deepfake videos should be a criminal offence.

item.title: Rivers run dry: How scorching summer shuts Europe's power plants, chokes supply chains
item.description: Extreme drought in Europe hinders economic growth and leads to severe measures. Romania closed its nuclear reactor due to low water levels, and Germany faces historical lows in the River Rhine, disrupting supply chains and contributing to inflationary pressures.

item.title: Michigan Democratic Senate primary results: Abdul El-Sayed projected to win after tight race against Haley Stevens
item.description: With more than 95% of ballots counted early Wednesday, El-Sayed held a slim lead of 48.6% to 47.3%. The Associated Press has not officially called the race.

item.title: Meta apologises for removing PM Modi's Facebook post, admits paid content boosting: Govt
item.description: Meta's global delegation, led by Global Affairs head Joel Kaplan, acknowledged lapses in the functioning of the company's platforms during its meeting with Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. Meta accepted errors related to platform operations.

item.title: Supreme Court says listening to youngsters is the ‘biggest powerful source’ to curb protest violence: ‘Forces should….'
item.description: The Supreme court observed that while maintaining law and order remains essential, the authorities should act with caution in dealing with such situations. It reiterated that acts such as stone-pelting could not be justified.

item.title: Centre orders joint probes into every suspected human rabies death
item.description: A new protocol mandates multi-agency investigations within 48 hours to trace infection sources, identify exposed contacts and strengthen rabies surveillance under the One Health framework.

item.title: Rural development ministry to use AI to rank states on audit performance
item.description: The rankings are expected to foster healthy competition among states while ensuring audit findings translate into measurable improvements in program delivery

item.title: Centre extends tenures of cabinet secretary, home secretary by a year
item.description: T. V. Somanathan and Govind Mohan have been given one-year service extensions as the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet clears their continued tenure.

item.title: Strongest El Nino since 1950 is on the way: What will be its impact on Indian monsoon?
item.description: A record-breaking El Nino event is expected in the tropical Pacific, influencing global weather patterns. It may cause droughts in Indonesia and Australia, impact India's monsoon, and lead to warmer winters in the Northern US, while pushing global temperatures to peak levels in 2026 and 2027.

item.title: He saved a drowning stranger by giving away his life jacket, then was swept away in Kerala floods
item.description: Rajesh, a native of Kalliyoor, was working as a rappelling instructor at Meenthully Waterfalls and had joined local volunteers responding to flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall on August 1.

item.title: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg apologises for CSAM, deepfake content, errors in operating platform: Report
item.description: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has apologised for child abuse content, deepfakes and errors in operating the platform, according to a report on Wednesday after a meeting between company's global team and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw.

item.title: Wind of change? Prince William and Kate don’t want their kids to face what Harry experienced, says royal family author
item.description: Prince William and Princess Kate Middleton are concerned about their younger children's royal futures, aiming to avoid past challenges faced by Prince Harry.&nbsp;

item.title: Centre raises FY27 apprenticeship target by 40%
item.description: The Centre also introduces a quality benchmark, requiring that at least 40% of apprentices be rated ‘good’ or above by the industries where they undergo training.

item.title: No foreign travel for Abhishek Banerjee: Calcutta High Court denies permission for eye treatment abroad
item.description: The Calcutta High Court denied Abhishek Banerjee permission for overseas eye treatment, dismissing his petition after he refused to appear before a medical board.&nbsp;

item.title: 'Grave security risk’: CJP's Saurav Das claims YouTubers 'broke' into his house; MP Derek O’Brien says raising it in RS
item.description: CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that YouTubers breached his privacy at his home, posing security risks to him and his family. He is attending a CJP meeting in Maharashtra. TMC MP Derk O’Brien plans to take up the issue in the Rajya Sabha.

item.title: No more fake paneer: Maharashtra bans analogue substitutes for a year; violators to face jail term and fine
item.description: The FSSAI defines analogue dairy products as non-milk constituents that resemble milk products. Maharashtra has banned analogue paneer for a year, imposing severe penalties for violations under the Food Safety Act, 2006, including possible life imprisonment for unsafe food that causes death.

item.title: Chandipura virus outbreak: Centre deploys national response team to Gujarat and Rajasthan
item.description: A multi-agency expert team has been sent to support field operations as Gujarat reports 22 child deaths, while scientists launch a major investigation into the virus's transmission cycle and genetic mutations.

item.title: Quote of the day by Thomas Henry Huxley: 'Try to learn something about everything and…'
item.description: With this quote, Thomas Henry Huxley reminds us that the most fulfilled and impactful individuals are those who remain curious about the world while striving for excellence in one particular field.

item.title: Ajit Agarkar may lose his job over Rohit Sharma’s retirement controversy; VVS Laxman likely to take over: Report
item.description: Rohit Sharma silenced retirement rumours by scoring 138 runs at Lord's, becoming the first Indian to achieve this milestone. Meanwhile, the future of chief selector Ajit Agarkar is uncertain.

item.title: Jharkhand hunger strike: Sonam Wangchuk urges Devendra Nath Mahato to drink water; Abhijeet Dipke says 'will ...'
item.description: The veteran educationist and activist, who himself was on a hunger strike for 26 days, asked Mahato to drink water as it otherwise will be 'tantamount to suicide'.

item.title: Quote Of The Day: Henry Ford's three-step formula for lasting success
item.description: Today's Quote of the Day comes from industrialist Henry Ford, whose famous words on teamwork continue to resonate in boardrooms, classrooms and workplaces alike. Here's what the quote means, the story behind it and why its message remains relevant in today's collaborative world.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg asked to apologise over PM Modi's reel fiasco; Parl panel warns Meta of losing legal protection if….
item.description: The Parliamentary Standing Committee asked Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to issue an apology with 3 days over Facebook's removal of a video featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The committee warned that failure to comply could result in the loss of legal immunity under Section 79 of the IT Act.
